reason: WebGL is single-threaded by default (no System.Threading.Thread). Requires the WebGL Threads/pthreads build option (SharedArrayBuffer + COOP/COEP headers) or must be refactored to use coroutines/async instead.
Background thread pool work is not available on standard WebGL builds.
Cross-thread synchronization primitives are meaningless without real threads on WebGL; usually a sign the code assumes a multi-threaded environment.
Blocking on Task.Wait()/.Result can deadlock in WebGL's single-threaded synchronization-context model since there is no background thread to complete the task. Prefer await/coroutines.
Launching external OS processes is impossible in a browser sandbox.
WebGL uses IL2CPP ahead-of-time compilation only; System.Reflection.Emit (runtime code generation) is not supported.
Raw TCP/UDP sockets are not available in browsers. Use UnityWebRequest (HTTP) or a WebSocket client instead.

Directory enumeration outside the virtual IDBFS persistentDataPath is unsupported on WebGL.
